These snippets are released under MIT-0: use them in any app, no attribution needed. Adapt names to the project, keep the logic.

## RN-001: Token or password stored in AsyncStorage, unencrypted MMKV, or redux-persist

Keep short-lived tokens in memory. Store long-lived tokens and passwords with react-native-keychain or expo-secure-store, which use the Android Keystore and the iOS Keychain. For MMKV, pass an `encryptionKey` that you generate once and keep in the Keychain or Keystore. For redux-persist, leave the auth slice out of `whitelist` or persist it through encrypted storage.

```ts
import * as SecureStore from 'expo-secure-store';

// Instead of AsyncStorage.setItem('authToken', token):
export async function saveToken(token: string): Promise<void> {
  await SecureStore.setItemAsync('authToken', token, {
    keychainAccessible: SecureStore.WHEN_UNLOCKED_THIS_DEVICE_ONLY,
  });
}

export function loadToken(): Promise<string | null> {
  return SecureStore.getItemAsync('authToken');
}
```

Verify: Sign in on an emulator, then run `adb shell run-as <package> ls -R databases files` and print the storage files (AsyncStorage uses `databases/RKStorage`, MMKV uses `files/mmkv`). Confirm no token or password appears in readable form.

Book: [§6.4](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/02-data-at-rest.md#64-the-uncomfortable-question-nobody-asked)

## RN-003: HTTP requests or responses are logged in every build

Add logging interceptors, redux-logger, and `startNetworkLogging()` only under `if (__DEV__)`. Log the method, URL, and status, never headers or bodies. Remove console calls from release builds with babel-plugin-transform-remove-console.

```ts
import axios from 'axios';

export const api = axios.create({ baseURL: 'https://api.example.com' });

if (__DEV__) {
  api.interceptors.request.use((config) => {
    console.log(config.method, config.url); // never the headers or the body
    return config;
  });
}
```

Verify: Install a release build, sign in, and watch `adb logcat` or Console.app: no request headers, tokens, or response bodies should appear.

Book: [§6.6](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/02-data-at-rest.md#66-how-to-implement-it)

## RN-004: JS networking library accepts any server certificate

Remove the option, or set it to `false`. For a local test server, trust its certificate in a debug-only network security config on Android or a debug-only trust setting on iOS. To pin certificates, pass `sslPinning: { certs: [...] }` to react-native-ssl-pinning, which keeps the normal checks.

```ts
import { fetch } from 'react-native-ssl-pinning';

export async function getProfile(): Promise<unknown> {
  const res = await fetch('https://api.example.com/profile', {
    method: 'GET',
    // api_example_com.cer ships in the app; the normal certificate checks stay on
    sslPinning: { certs: ['api_example_com'] },
    headers: { Accept: 'application/json' },
  });
  return res.json();
}
```

Verify: Send the app's traffic through a proxy whose CA the phone doesn't trust, and confirm these requests fail.

Book: [§7.1](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/03-data-in-transit.md#71-the-baseline)

## RN-005: WebView can read local files

Remove `allowFileAccess`, `allowFileAccessFromFileURLs` and `allowUniversalAccessFromFileURLs`. They are off by default. Pass bundled HTML with `source={{ html }}` or `require()`. On iOS, point `allowingReadAccessToURL` at the one folder that holds the page.

```tsx
// File access stays off: these are the react-native-webview defaults.
<WebView
  source={require('./help.html')}   // or source={{ html: helpHtml }}
  allowFileAccess={false}
  allowFileAccessFromFileURLs={false}
  allowUniversalAccessFromFileURLs={false}
/>
```

Verify: Load a page that runs `fetch('file:///data/data/<your.package>/shared_prefs/')` and confirm the request fails.

Book: [§16.3](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/07-platform-surfaces-and-new-frontiers.md#163-file-access-the-setting-nobody-remembers-changing)

## RN-006: WebView may navigate to any origin or URL scheme

Remove `originWhitelist` to keep the default (http and https), or list the exact origins you own, such as `['https://app.example.com']`. Keep `['*']` only for a WebView that shows your own HTML string.

```tsx
<WebView
  source={{ uri: 'https://app.example.com/help' }}
  // Only these origins load inside the app. Other URLs go to the system, which opens them outside it.
  originWhitelist={['https://app.example.com', 'https://help.example.com']}
/>
```

Verify: From the page, navigate to a URL outside the list and confirm the WebView doesn't load it inside the app.

Book: [§16.4](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/07-platform-surfaces-and-new-frontiers.md#164-loading-untrusted-content)

## RN-007: WebView loads a URL from navigation params or user input with no allowlist

Parse the URL with `new URL()`, require https, and compare the hostname with an exact allowlist before you render the WebView. Run the same check in `onShouldStartLoadWithRequest`.

```tsx
const ALLOWED_HOSTS = new Set(['app.example.com', 'help.example.com']);

// Older React Native versions need react-native-url-polyfill for URL.hostname.
function isAllowed(url: string): boolean {
  try {
    const u = new URL(url);
    return u.protocol === 'https:' && ALLOWED_HOSTS.has(u.hostname);
  } catch {
    return false;
  }
}

export function HelpScreen({ route }) {
  const url = route.params?.url;
  if (!url || !isAllowed(url)) return null;
  return (
    <WebView
      source={{ uri: url }}
      onShouldStartLoadWithRequest={(req) => isAllowed(req.url)}
    />
  );
}
```

Verify: Open the screen with `https://evil.example/` as its URL param and confirm the WebView refuses it.

Book: [§16.4](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/07-platform-surfaces-and-new-frontiers.md#164-loading-untrusted-content)

## RN-008: WebView bridge trusts the page

In `onMessage`, check `new URL(event.nativeEvent.url).origin` against your origin, then validate the message. Send data to the page with `postMessage`, or encode it with `JSON.stringify` before you put it in a script.

```tsx
const APP_ORIGIN = 'https://app.example.com';

function onMessage(event: WebViewMessageEvent) {
  // 1. Who sent it? Act only on messages from your own page.
  let origin = '';
  try { origin = new URL(event.nativeEvent.url).origin; } catch { return; }
  if (origin !== APP_ORIGIN) return;

  // 2. What did it send? Untrusted input.
  let msg: { type?: unknown };
  try { msg = JSON.parse(event.nativeEvent.data); } catch { return; }
  if (msg.type === 'close') closeScreen();
}

// Send data to the page as a message, never as script text.
webViewRef.current?.postMessage(JSON.stringify({ userName }));
```

Verify: Load a page from another origin, call `window.ReactNativeWebView.postMessage(...)` from it, and confirm the app ignores the message.

Book: [§16.2](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/07-platform-surfaces-and-new-frontiers.md#162-the-javascript-bridge-and-why-its-the-sharpest-edge)

## RN-009: Deep-link data reaches openURL, fetch, a WebView, or navigation without an allowlist

Parse the link with `new URL()` and compare `protocol` and `hostname` to a fixed allowlist before using it. Map link paths to screen names and plain IDs, never to raw URLs.

```ts
import { Linking } from 'react-native';

const ALLOWED_HOSTS = new Set(['example.com', 'help.example.com']);

function safeTarget(raw: string | null): URL | null {
  try {
    const u = new URL(raw ?? '');
    return u.protocol === 'https:' && ALLOWED_HOSTS.has(u.hostname) ? u : null;
  } catch {
    return null;
  }
}

Linking.addEventListener('url', ({ url }) => {
  const target = safeTarget(new URL(url).searchParams.get('next'));
  if (target) Linking.openURL(target.toString());
});
```

Verify: Open `myapp://open?next=https://evil.example` (or `adb shell am start -d '<link>'` on Android). The app should refuse it and stay on a safe screen.

Book: [§17.5](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/07-platform-surfaces-and-new-frontiers.md#175-deep-links-and-the-verification-that-makes-them-safe)

## RN-010: JavaScript code is built from a string at runtime

Remove the runtime code. Parse data with `JSON.parse`, pick behavior from a fixed map of functions, and pass functions, not strings, to `setTimeout` and `setInterval`.

```ts
// Data, not code: parse it, then choose behavior from a fixed map.
const actions: Record<string, (p: unknown) => void> = { refresh, logout };
const msg = JSON.parse(text);
const run = actions[msg.type];
if (run) run(msg.payload);

// A function, not a string.
setTimeout(() => refresh(), 1000);
```

Verify: Search the app's own code for `eval(`, `Function(`, and `setTimeout(` with a string. No call should take text that is built at runtime.

Book: [§19.3](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/07-platform-surfaces-and-new-frontiers.md#193-injection-the-shape-of-the-bug)

## RN-011: SQLite query built by joining strings

Write `?` placeholders in the SQL and pass the values in the parameters array (`executeSql(sql, [a, b])`, `runAsync(sql, a, b)`). Pick table, column, and sort names from a fixed list.

```ts
import * as SQLite from 'expo-sqlite';

const db = await SQLite.openDatabaseAsync('app.db');
// Values go in the parameters, never in the SQL text.
const rows = await db.getAllAsync('SELECT * FROM notes WHERE folder = ? AND title LIKE ?', folderId, `%${term}%`);
```

Verify: Pass a value such as `' OR '1'='1` through the code path and confirm the query treats it as plain text.

Book: [§19.3](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/07-platform-surfaces-and-new-frontiers.md#193-injection-the-shape-of-the-bug)

## RN-012: React Native biometric check only returns a boolean

Keep the secret in an item that only biometric authentication releases: react-native-keychain with `accessControl: ACCESS_CONTROL.BIOMETRY_CURRENT_SET`, or expo-secure-store with `requireAuthentication: true`. Or sign a server challenge with react-native-biometrics `createSignature`.

```ts
import * as Keychain from 'react-native-keychain';

await Keychain.setGenericPassword('session', token, {
  accessControl: Keychain.ACCESS_CONTROL.BIOMETRY_CURRENT_SET,
  accessible: Keychain.ACCESSIBLE.WHEN_PASSCODE_SET_THIS_DEVICE_ONLY,
});
// The OS shows the prompt; the token is released only after a real match.
const creds = await Keychain.getGenericPassword({ authenticationPrompt: { title: 'Unlock' } });
```

Verify: Hook the prompt to return success with Frida (`frida -U -f <app>`). The protected data should stay locked, because no key was released.

Book: [§11.1](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/04-proving-who-is-calling.md#111-decorative-versus-real)

## RN-013: crypto-js derives the AES key from a passphrase string

Pass a random 256-bit key as a WordArray, kept in the Keychain or Keystore (for example through react-native-keychain), with a random IV for each message. Better, use native AES-GCM. If the key must come from a password, use PBKDF2 with SHA-256 and at least 600,000 iterations.

```ts
import CryptoJS from 'crypto-js';

// rawKeyHex: 32 random bytes, generated once and kept in the Keychain/Keystore.
const key = CryptoJS.enc.Hex.parse(rawKeyHex);
const iv = CryptoJS.lib.WordArray.random(16);          // new for every message
const ct = CryptoJS.AES.encrypt(plaintext, key, { iv });
const stored = iv.toString() + ':' + ct.toString();     // keep the IV with the ciphertext
```

Verify: Search for `AES.encrypt(` and `AES.decrypt(`. Each call should get a WordArray key and an `iv` option, never a string.

Book: [Chapter 0.2](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/00-foundations.md#chapter-02-cryptography-you-actually-need)

## RN-014: Over-the-air JavaScript updates are not signature-checked

For expo-updates, generate a key pair with `npx expo-updates codesigning:generate`, then set `updates.codeSigningCertificate` and `updates.codeSigningMetadata` and sign each update. For CodePush, release with a private key and add `CodePushPublicKey` to Info.plist and strings.xml.

```json
{
  "expo": {
    "updates": {
      "url": "https://u.expo.dev/<project-id>",
      "codeSigningCertificate": "./certs/certificate.pem",
      "codeSigningMetadata": { "keyid": "main", "alg": "rsa-v1_5-sha256" }
    }
  }
}
```

Verify: Publish an update without the signature (or with a different key) to a test channel, and confirm the app refuses it and keeps running the embedded bundle.

Book: [§19.5](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/07-platform-surfaces-and-new-frontiers.md#195-dynamic-code-loading)

## RN-015: JavaScript console output ships in release builds

Add `babel-plugin-transform-remove-console` to the production env of your babel config (keep `error` and `warn` if you need them), or set metro's `minifierConfig.compress.drop_console` to true. Wrap the remaining debug logging in `if (__DEV__)`.

```js
// babel.config.js
module.exports = {
  presets: ['module:@react-native/babel-preset'],
  env: {
    production: {
      plugins: [['transform-remove-console', { exclude: ['error', 'warn'] }]],
    },
  },
};
```

Verify: Build a release bundle with `npx react-native bundle --dev false` (or `npx expo export`), and confirm `grep -c console.log` on the output finds none of your own log lines.

Book: [§6.6](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/02-data-at-rest.md#66-how-to-implement-it)

## RN-016: Hermes is turned off

Turn Hermes back on: `hermesEnabled=true` in android/gradle.properties, remove `:hermes_enabled => false` from the Podfile, and remove `"jsEngine": "jsc"` from app.json. Hermes is the default since React Native 0.70.

```properties
# android/gradle.properties
hermesEnabled=true
```

Verify: Unzip the release APK and run `xxd -l 4 assets/index.android.bundle`: a Hermes bundle starts with the bytes `c61f bc03`, while a JavaScript bundle starts with readable text.

Book: [§14.3](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/05-resilience.md#143-where-obfuscation-genuinely-helps)

## RN-018: Debug tooling connects in release builds

Start the tool only inside `if (__DEV__) { ... }`, and load its config file with `if (__DEV__) require('./ReactotronConfig')`. Keep `developmentClient: true` out of store build profiles in eas.json.

```js
// index.js
if (__DEV__) {
  require('./ReactotronConfig');
}
```

Verify: Build a release bundle and search it for `reactotron`, `flipper`, and `remotedev`: none should be found, and the app should open no connection to port 9090 or 8000.

## RN-019: npm dependencies can be swapped at the source or in transit

Pin git dependencies to a full commit SHA, or publish them to a registry. Use version ranges with a committed lockfile. Use an https registry, keep `strict-ssl` and `enableStrictSsl` on, and read registry tokens from the environment, for example `_authToken=${NPM_TOKEN}`.

```ini
# .npmrc: an https registry, TLS checks on, and the token read from the environment
registry=https://registry.npmjs.org/
strict-ssl=true
//registry.npmjs.org/:_authToken=${NPM_TOKEN}
```

Verify: Check that every git dependency in package.json ends in `#` and a 40-character commit SHA, and that .npmrc and .yarnrc.yml have no `http://` registry, no `false` TLS setting, and no literal token. Then run `npm ci` or `yarn install --immutable` on a clean checkout.

Book: [§15.4](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/06-the-build-and-release-pipeline.md#154-dependencies-and-build-inputs)

## RN-020: Native module runs a shell command or opens a file path sent from JavaScript

Remove generic `exec` and `readFile` bridge methods. Expose only the specific action the app needs, take a name from a fixed list instead of a path, and check that the resolved canonical path stays inside the app's folder.

```kotlin
@ReactMethod
fun readConfig(name: String, promise: Promise) {
    val allowed = setOf("theme", "locale")            // names, not paths
    if (name !in allowed) { promise.reject("E_DENIED", "not allowed"); return }
    val base = File(reactApplicationContext.filesDir, "config").canonicalFile
    val file = File(base, "$name.json").canonicalFile
    if (!file.path.startsWith(base.path + File.separator)) { promise.reject("E_DENIED", "bad path"); return }
    promise.resolve(file.readText())
}
```

Verify: Call the method from JavaScript with `../../databases/app.db` or `id; ls`. It should refuse both.

Book: [§19.3](https://github.com/hossam9k/mobile-app-security/blob/main/book/07-platform-surfaces-and-new-frontiers.md#193-injection-the-shape-of-the-bug)
